title_original: A Better Way to Do Black Friday
excerpt_original: Artists, artisans, and small presses to support in the face of capitalism’s deluge, Oswaldo Vigas at the Guangdong Museum, and how ’bout a Hyperallergic membership this holiday season?

blocks.text: I don’t know about you, but I feel like the Black Friday promotion emails (and, increasingly, text messages) are getting more and more unhinged, rising to a never-ending din of discount codes and cringey marketing copy that’s making me consider hibernation until January 1. But there’s a better way, and it doesn’t involve another final-sale item that looked great online but fits you like a paper bag. Today, Staff Writer Anna Lee brings us a cornucopia of artist-centered alternatives, from genre-bending publications by small presses to stunning beadwork from Native trading posts and highly giftable artist editions (someone get me those David Shrigley salt shakers!)

And if you’re looking for a thoughtful and personal gift that gives back, why not a Hyperallergic membership for your MFA-grad BFF or museum-hopping mother-in-law (or that one uncle with the bad politics you’re hoping to de-influence)? You’ll get unlimited access to the site, invites to exclusive events, commenting privileges, and the joy of knowing you’re supporting our work as one of very few surviving independent arts publications.
Also today, Madeleine Seidel on a major survey dedicated to Oswaldo Vigas, the Venezuelan artist curator Gabriela Rangel calls an "amphibian modernist," and much more.
—Valentina Di Liscia, senior editor
This Black Friday, Shop From Artists and Art Nonprofits

From high-end brands shaving deceptively large sums off their already price-hiked catalogs to the ye olde tradition of department stores luring families in with a handsome deal, Black Friday is every American corporation’s wet dream. Here at Hyperallergic, we encourage you to dig a little deeper into your purses this year for the independent retailers, artists, and nonprofits out there. You (and your loved ones) will be pleasantly surprised by the gems you find on our list of small businesses, imprints, print shops, and Native American trading posts to keep on your radar this holiday season. | Anna Lee
